dek: A handicapper who started as a ghost writer in 2000 and began selling picks in 2009. His plays sit inside the SportsLine and VegasInsider subscriptions, which cost $13.99 to $19.99 a month, and he also sells packages of his own on CappersPicks, from $99 for 3 days to $1,999.95 for a year. Every record shown for him is graded by a site that sells his picks, and we found almost no independent buyer talk.

short_answer: Zack Cimini is a real, active handicapper. SportsLine lists him as an expert with a dated pick list, with graded picks as recent as 19 Nov 2026, VegasInsider has a profile and ranks him on its best handicappers page, and CBS Sports was already citing his baseball runs in 2018. On 20 Nov 2026 he also had a sales page on CappersPicks, part of the SportsCapping network, with packages of his own.

That gives buyers two very different prices for what appear to be the same plays. On SportsLine his picks come with every other expert for $13.99 a month. On CappersPicks a 3 day pass was $99.00 and a year $1,999.95. The two plays in CappersPicks' yesterday table for 19 Nov 2026 were the same games and sides as two of his SportsLine picks that night.

The records published for him are mostly consistent with the arithmetic. SportsLine's football and college basketball lines work out to 54% to 57% winners, and its all time line of 1060-1015-8 to about 51% that still shows a profit because many baseball picks are plus money. The windows are chosen by the sellers, the SportsLine bio still says "Entering the 2027 MLB season", and the CappersPicks page carries season lines that look out of date.

Independent buyer comment is close to nonexistent. We found no Reddit thread, forum review or complaint about him, and the only outside mentions were pick sharing accounts reposting his plays. Treat him as a media handicapper with house graded records, not a proven long term winner.

guarantee: SportsLine offers no guarantee on his picks. His profile says the content is "for entertainment purposes only" and that SportsLine makes no guarantee about the accuracy of its information or the outcome of any game. The SportsLine terms of use say a subscription "will automatically renew and be charged to your Payment Method at the then current rate", that cancellation takes effect at the end of the period, and in capitals: "YOU WILL NOT RECEIVE A REFUND OF ANY FEES PAID."
The VegasInsider premium page has no refund or guarantee wording at all, and its $4.99 3 Day Pass turns into a $19.99 monthly plan unless you cancel.

CappersPicks marks his 3 day, 7 day and 1 year packages "GUARANTEED". Its policy page says "Cappers Picks handicappers guarantee their subscriptions with site credit equal to the amount of the purchase", that "This guarantee applies only to losing subscriptions", and that eligibility is judged on betting profit graded at "the odds selected by the handicapper when the pick is published." The page says the policy dates from December 2016 and tells buyers to confirm it is still in effect. That is site credit, not money back.
Losses on the bets themselves are never covered by any of the three sites.

claims_note: How we checked: we read his SportsLine profile and MLB tab, his VegasInsider profile and the CappersPicks and Capper Reviews pages on 20 Nov 2026, recomputed each win percentage from the wins and losses shown (pushes left out), estimated what each SportsLine record would return at standard -110 prices, and counted the 15 graded picks shown on SportsLine ourselves.

The SportsLine figures hold together better than most sellers' runs: the football and college basketball dollar figures are close to what the records would return at normal prices. They are still graded by SportsLine, which sells the subscription.

The VegasInsider list is a set of best finishes from selected seasons, and its profile still showed two featured pick cards filled with template text such as "My Pick Title (XXX)". The CappersPicks page mixes current plays with season lines and rankings that appear to date from an earlier season, and includes a 2015 ranking.

Same plays, different prices: CappersPicks' yesterday table for 19 Nov 2026 listed Tulane +2.5 at -115 (a loss) and the Knicks at -102 (a win). SportsLine listed Tulane +2.5 at -115 and the Knicks -1.5 at +100 the same night. A buyer paying $99 for 3 days on CappersPicks may be getting plays that a $13.99 SportsLine month also includes.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Zack Cimini does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Zack Cimini most often were TheGodOfCappers, BettingBuddyy, 1218Sports, EZMSports. From 26 Sep 2026 to 10 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Zack Cimini block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 2 plays, 2 won, 0 lost, +1.80 units, a return of +90.1% per unit risked. By month: September 1 won, 0 lost, +0.89 units; November 1 won, 0 lost, +0.91 units.
What it means: 2 decided plays is far too few to judge.
What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no third party tracker or contest record covering a long run of his picks, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the sellers publish: SportsLine lists his recent picks with the date, the bet, the odds, the unit size and the result, plus a last 60 MLB money line widget showing 34-26-0. CappersPicks shows a yesterday table and a 7 day board that had him at 8-3 for $463 on 20 Nov 2026. VegasInsider shows leaderboard finishes for selected seasons. Each site sells the picks it grades.

Background: VegasInsider and CappersPicks say he began in 2000 as a freelance ghost writer for a Las Vegas based company, at 16 by the CappersPicks account, and became a handicapper in 2009. CappersPicks credits him with futures winners such as UConn at 40 to 1 in February 2011 and the Giants at 40 to 1 in November 2010; we could not check these. CBS Sports cited a 132-100 baseball run for him in September 2018. VegasInsider was bought by Better Collective, a sports betting affiliate company, in July 2019 for $20 million.

our_data.text: In this edition no Zack Cimini pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Zack Cimini performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the SportsLine all time figure of 1060-1015-8 works out to about 51% winners, in profit on the page because many MLB bets are at plus money.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Zack Cimini is very thin. Because he is one expert inside large subscription sites, buyers talk about SportsLine or VegasInsider as a whole, not about him.

customers.text: We found no buyer review, complaint or forum thread about Zack Cimini on Reddit, Covers, Sportsbook Review or TheRX, and no news or regulator record. The only outside mentions are a handful of posts on X from September to November 2026: pick sharing accounts reposting his SportsLine plays next to other cappers, one under a "5-0 in last 5 NFL ATS picks" heading, and one tracking account praising an 18 and 12 run over 30 picks. Nobody we found described buying from him, good or bad. His Capper Reviews page, run by the network that sells his CappersPicks packages, has 2 votes and no comments, and SportsLine's member testimonial page does not mention him. There is no smoke here either way; there is simply very little talk.

Capper Reviews rates him 3.00 out of 5 from 2 votes, with no written comments. The page says he sells picks through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of, so the rating is not independent and two votes mean little.

CappersPicks' 7 day board listed him at 8-3 for $463, and his sales page calls him "one of the more prominent handicappers in the country." CappersPicks sells his packages and grades the picks, so this is marketing.
SportsLine's member testimonial page from May 2024 shares member success stories but does not mention him.

Our saved copy of ten betting subreddits from 2024 to 2026 has no mention of him, and live Reddit archive searches for cimini found no posts in r/sportsbook or r/SportsBettingPicks on 16 Nov and timed out on 20 Nov. Web searches found no Covers, Sportsbook Review or TheRX thread about him, and no Better Business Bureau or news coverage beyond his own sellers.

conflicts: SportsLine, VegasInsider and CappersPicks each sell access to his picks, grade them and publish his records. The best handicappers page that praises him sits on VegasInsider, and the CBS Sports article citing his 2018 run promoted SportsLine, which CBS owns.

VegasInsider has been owned since 2019 by Better Collective, a sports betting affiliate company, and its best handicappers page promotes sportsbook bonus codes and says the site "contains commercial content." Affiliates are usually paid when readers sign up and bet.

CappersPicks lists offshore sportsbook bonus codes beside his packages, says the network's records are "DOCUMENTED", and states that "Cappers Picks are located in Antigua, West Indies." Capper Reviews, which rates him, is part of the same network.
The same plays appear to be sold at very different prices on different sites, which a buyer cannot see from any one page.
strengths: SportsLine shows each recent pick with the date, odds, unit size and result, which is more than most pick sellers publish.
The SportsLine records are arithmetically consistent: the dollar figures are close to what the win and loss records would return at normal prices.
Low prices for what you get on SportsLine: $13.99 a month includes every expert on the site.
Mostly small, steady stakes of 0.5 or 1 unit, and no game of the year pitches on SportsLine or VegasInsider.
A long, visible career: CBS Sports cited his baseball run in 2018 and his bios trace him back to 2009.
concerns: Every record is graded by a site that sells the picks. We found no outside audit or long third party track.
The all time SportsLine line is about 51% winners and under 2% return on money risked, in profit only through plus money prices a buyer may not get after a line moves.
The same plays appear to sell for $13.99 a month on SportsLine and $99 for 3 days on CappersPicks.
Out of date or unfinished pages: the SportsLine bio refers to the 2027 MLB season, VegasInsider showed template text, and CappersPicks shows season lines and a 2015 ranking.
Plans renew automatically, SportsLine gives no refunds, and the CappersPicks guarantee is site credit only.
Almost no independent buyer feedback exists, positive or negative.
checklist: If you want his picks, compare prices first: a SportsLine month costs less than a single CappersPicks 3 day pass.
Open his SportsLine profile and read the full pick list with odds and units, not just the headline lines.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 51% record can only profit through plus money prices you may not get.
Set a reminder to cancel before any auto renewal, and remember the VegasInsider $4.99 pass becomes $19.99 a month.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper whose picks are sold through SportsLine, part of CBS, VegasInsider and CappersPicks. We found no complaints, court cases or regulator actions about him. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records come from the sites that sell them.
What does the Watchdog sample of Zack Cimini show?
We graded 2 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 26 Sep 2026 to 10 Nov 2026: 2 won, 0 lost, +1.80 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
How much does Zack Cimini cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 SportsLine cost $13.99 a month, $39.99 for 3 months or $139.99 a year, and VegasInsider $19.99 a month, $119.99 a year or $4.99 for a 3 day pass that renews at $19.99 a month; both include every expert. CappersPicks sold his picks alone from $99.00 for 3 days to $1,999.95 for a year.
Are his picks the same on every site?

They appear to overlap. The two plays CappersPicks listed for him on 19 Nov 2026 were the same games and sides as two of his SportsLine picks that night, at nearly the same prices. We could not compare full lists, because each site shows only part of its history.
Does Zack Cimini offer refunds or a guarantee?

SportsLine's terms say no refunds of fees paid, and VegasInsider shows no refund wording. CappersPicks guarantees some packages with site credit equal to the purchase if the subscription loses money, not cash back.
Does Zack Cimini have a verified record?

No outside audit exists. SportsLine publishes a dated pick list and records such as 1060-1015-8 all time and 91-68-2 in college football over three seasons, and VegasInsider and CappersPicks list rankings, but all are graded by the sellers.

On SportsLine the price is low and the pick history is more open than most. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the market over hundreds of plays at the prices you can actually get, and nothing refunds the subscription or your betting losses.
